newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran quake toll 930, thousands injured - state media.
newsitem.headline: Iran quake toll 930, thousands injured - state media.

text.p: Nearly 1,000 people were killed and thousands injured on Saturday when an earthquake devastated eastern Iran, state media said.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA, giving the latest death toll, said more than 800 people were killed in the area of Qaen and 130 villagers had died in the vicinity of the town of Birjand.
Both are in the south of Khorasan province, epicentre of the quake which measured 7.1 on the Richter scale.
There was confusion over the number of injured. IRNA said 5,000 were hurt but Tehran radio put the figure at 40,000 and Iranian television said the number was in the thousands.
The radio said there was a dire need for medical and surgical personnel, medicine, blood, tents, food, ambulances, heavy earth-moving equipment and helicopters.
It said electricity and water supplies to villages in the quake zone had been cut off and water and other relief supplies were being transported to the stricken region.
IRNA quoted an official in the town of Qaen near the quake's epicentre as saying 80 of the region's 150 villages suffered 80 percent destruction and the others were heavily damaged.
The injured were being rushed to hospitals in five nearby towns and cities, the official said. The area under his jurisdiction has a population of more than 40,000.
Iranian television said thousands of people in the rural region known for its saffron production were made homeless by the quake, which was felt across four provinces.

Heavy damage was also inflicted on Qaen and Birjand near the epicentre 150 km (90 miles) from the border with Afghanistan said Mehdi Siadati, head of the disaster relief agency in Darmian district of Khorasan province.
He told IRNA that teams had been rushed to stricken areas and a headquarters had been set up to manage relief operations.

Some 30 aftershocks ranging in strength from 3.5 to 5.5 on the Richter scale shook Birjand within four hours of the earthquake and more were expected, said the Geophysics Institute at the city of Mashhad, which was jolted by the first tremor.

It recorded the epicentre 370 km (230 miles) southeast of Mashhad, Iran's second largest city with a population of about two million. The quake, which struck at 12:28 p.m. (0758 GMT), was felt up to 800 km (500 miles) away, IRNA reported.

The television said Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei asked the top clerical official in Khorasan province to use all necessary resources from the province's large religious endowments to help the quake victims.

The stricken area is significantly less densely populated than a region near the Caspian Sea coast where 35,000 people were killed by an earthquake measuring 7.3 in 1990. That was the worst recorded jolt to hit quake-prone Iran.
At least 1,000 people were killed and more than 36,000 made homeless when a quake measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale hit northwest Iran in February.
IRNA said the latest quake caused panic as far away as the city of Kashan south of the capital Tehran, where people said they saw water in ponds spill over.
A journalist in Mashhad, capital of Iran's northeastern Khorasan province bordering Afghanistan and Turkmenistan, said there was no apparent widespread damage in the city.

The U.S. Geological Survey based in Golden, Colorado measured the quake at 7.3 on the Richter scale at its epicentre. U.S. geophysicist Waverly Person said its focus was fairly shallow -- about 20 miles (30 km) below the earth's surface.
